blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Because the Earth is spherical, circles drawn around it without intersecting stay parallel.
Lines of latitude never meet at any point.
Unlike latitudes, longitudes do intersect and are not parallel.
Latitudes are parallel lines that never intersect, which distinguishes them from longitudes.
The spherical shape of the Earth is the primary reason why latitudes can be drawn as non-intersecting parallel circles.
